d7b5c1b5-65bd-45b4-99ae-46de47271b73.title: Cult-Classic PS3, Xbox 360 Game Getting New Sequel After 14 Years
d7b5c1b5-65bd-45b4-99ae-46de47271b73.incipit: A cult-classic game that originally launched on PS3 and Xbox 360 platforms has been confirmed to be getting a new sequel after 14 years. In the last full year of the PS3 and Xbox 360 generation, a number of...
d7b5c1b5-65bd-45b4-99ae-46de47271b73.body:
A cult-classic game that originally launched on PS3 and Xbox 360 platforms has been confirmed to be getting a new sequel after 14 years. In the last full year of the PS3 and Xbox 360 generation, a number of iconic games came to each platform. Titles such as Borderlands 2 , Far Cry 3 , Mass Effect 3 , Dishonored , Telltale’s The Walking Dead , and Assassin’s Creed 3 came to both consoles in 2012, alongside countless others.

Now, one beloved action game that also launched in this same year is set to make a return on modern hardware with a sequel that many have been clamoring to see for quite some time. Announced this week by Dragami Games to coincide with TGS 2026, the publisher revealed that it’s now developing a sequel to Lollipop Chainsaw . Originally developed by Grasshopper Manufacture, Lollipop Chainsaw released in June 2012 to somewhat middling reviews from critics. However, the game’s outlandish concept that sees a high school cheerleader taking on hordes of zombies while equipped with a chainsaw ended up being quite popular with fans, resulting in Lollipop Chainsaw becoming a cult-classic.

As for this long-awaited sequel, the game is officially titled Lollipop Chainsaw 2: Back2Back . Details on this follow-up are still pretty slim, but Dragami Games did share some in-development footage of the project (which you can view below) to give fans an idea of what to expect. Based on this gameplay, Lollipop Chainsaw 2 is still very early in its creation, which means that it could be pretty far down the road, even if Dragami is claiming it’ll be out in 2027.

Still, the fact that it’s being made at all is equal parts surprising and exciting. Don’t Get Too Excited About This Sequel Just Yet If there is one concern to have with Lollipop Chainsaw 2 , it’s that the game isn’t being made by the team behind the original. While Dragami Games did work on the remastered version of the first entry, officially titled Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP , Grasshopper Manufacture isn’t involved whatsoever. This is a pretty major deal, especially considering that Grasshopper’s iconic director, Goichi “Suda51” Suda, was the creative lead behind Lollipop Chainsaw . In addition, famed writer/director James Gunn, who happened to co-write the original Lollipop Chainsaw , isn’t involved whatsoever with this sequel.

This shouldn’t be a shock in the slightest given that Gunn is now the head of DC Studios, but it’s yet another reason to have doubts about this new installment since so many of the creators behind the original have nothing to do with it this time around. As mentioned, Dragami Games is currently claiming that Lollipop Chainsaw 2 will be out next year, but we’ll see if this ends up holding true. Whenever we learn more about the game, we’ll be sure to update you here on ComicBook .

bd077b10-45af-43c3-a1a7-6369f272a32a.title: 4 Classic Gaming Franchises That Should Be Rebooted in a New Genre Like StarCraft
bd077b10-45af-43c3-a1a7-6369f272a32a.incipit: The StarCraft games have always been real-time strategy titles, but BlizzCon 2026 revealed that the upcoming 2030 reboot of StarCraft is set to be something different. Instead of a classic RTS with rival...
bd077b10-45af-43c3-a1a7-6369f272a32a.body:
The StarCraft games have always been real-time strategy titles, but BlizzCon 2026 revealed that the upcoming 2030 reboot of StarCraft is set to be something different. Instead of a classic RTS with rival armies, players will embody an individual role within an open world, third-person shooter, driven by a narrative closer to modern titles. This represents an interesting re-invention of the StarCraft series in some ways, reflecting how franchises can offer alternate angles at their settings beyond what players are used to.

This strategy doesn’t have to be exclusive to Blizzard’s RTS juggernaut, though, as other series have also seen success branching off into other genres. Whether it’s a spin-off game or a brand-new direction, some titles have captured new and old audiences alike by taking paths that feel refreshing. For example, Final Fantasy 7 Remake ‘s shift into real-time action, Halo ‘s change into an RTS for Halo Wars , or Fallout 3 becoming an open world RPG instead of a top-down CRPG have helped make those series more appealing through their evolution or variety. 4. Halo – RPG The Halo series is experimenting with reboots right now, with Halo: Campaign Evolved being a modern remake of the franchise’s blockbuster beginnings, but to mixed results.

While Halo Infinite and Campaign Evolved have pushed the boundaries on player expectations, the series used to be more willing to spin off from its mainline games. If the studios behind Halo want to keep jumping into the past, perhaps a game where players have more immersion in the world would be best, similar to StarCraft (2030) . An RPG similar to Fallout: New Vegas set in the world of Halo could be a fascinating departure for the series, where players get to customize their own Spartan or other human solider.

Alternatively, players might be able to create their own Sangheili, or Elite, during the era where they are fighting humans or allied with them after the events of Halo 3 . This type of game could be set at any point of the Halo time line, with an original story that gives players far greater creative control over the events that take place. Instead of a linear FPS campaign, the story of a Halo RPG could be a solider having to recruit a party of allies, perhaps from both sides of the series’ Covenant vs Humans conflict, to stop a greater threat. The parasitic Flood has always been an enemy that could unite various sides, but perhaps the RPG elements would only manifest in an individual character players control. Elements from Cyberpunk 2077 , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, or the Deus Ex games may lend some inspiration here, taking Halo in a fresh and interesting direction. 3.

Splinter Cell – First-Person Shooter (FPS) Image courtesy of Ubisoft The third-person stealth action of the Splinter Cell games are beloved by many, with the series being at the top of most peoples’ lists when it comes to “franchises that need to come back.” However, with the popularity of the latest Hitman games and the success of 007 First Light , which adopt Splinter Cell ‘s formula well, it may be better for the original series to branch off into a different idea. One way Splinter Cell could return is not as a game competing with Metal Gear Solid , but rather as a first-person shooter (FPS) with its emphasis on stealth intact. Almost like the Outlast horror games, players might find more immersion in the night vision of Splinter Cell through a first-person perspective. Games like the iconic Thief put players in first-person to make them think about their environments more, a message that would translate perfectly into the tactical missions of Splinter Cell too.

Although some players might argue that Rainbow Six Siege and its related games are enough for Tom Clancy FPS titles, having Splinter Cell go down a different route would help it stand out. To make this kind of game work, enemy AI would have to be improved, with more tactical mechanics being implemented to help players too. However, this might make Splinter Cell more authentic to its premise than it’s ever been before, with limitations to third-person action making the series more “action” than “stealth” oriented at times.

Slower movement and smaller environments would also help a Splinter Cell FPS thrive, especially if open-ended level design carries over from the series’ roots. 2. BioShock – Metroidvania The BioShock games will likely get reboots in the next few years, but the first-person action-adventure series could also receive a spin-off during that wait. Although many would argue for another FPS with RPG elements, the world building of BioShock could work well with genres that promote exploration, such as a Metroidvania. Imagining the underwater world of Rapture, or even BioShock Infinite ‘s high flying metropolis, in a vast and layered side scrolling game may be an enticing way to bring the series forward.

A Metroidvania BioShock game could introduce a brand-new world to players as well, allowing them to explore a location completely devoid of reference for a fresh experience. Some of the series’ main features, such as DNA-altering powers, would be easy to bring back as part of the game’s exploration to unlock new progression paths. At the same time, the game could do what other Metroidvanias, like Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse are doing right now, by allowing players to create “loadouts” with various abilities.

This would align the BioShock Metroidvania with the FPS games somewhat, making the game feel different, yet still a BioShock entry. The popularity of games like Hollow Knight: Silksong or upcoming titles like Metroid Ravenous shows how big Metroidvanias are right now, especially if their settings captivate players. BioShock has one of the most interesting gaming locations of all time, so traveling to different Metroidvania “rooms” or biomes in its settings wouldn’t be boring by any stretch. With other series jumping into Metroidvanias with some success, such as The Prince of Persia , BioShock may work well outside its FPS approach. 1. Dino Crisis – Over-the-Shoulder Third-Person Shooter One of the most underrated survival horror series out there is Dino Crisis , a Capcom game where players have to fight against dinosaurs while scrounging for resources.

This game is long overdue for a reboot, but its fixed camera angles are a stamp for that era of survival horror, building off the same philosophies established by the Resident Evil series. Much like that Capcom franchise evolved, so too can Dino Crisis become stronger by doing the same thing Resident Evil 4 did. That game changed fixed cameras to an over-the-shoulder style of third-person action, putting players up close and personal with the dangers they were facing. This direction would work extra well for Dino Crisis , as the sheer size and scale of the dinosaurs in that game would be easier to capture through that intimacy.

Already, games like Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis (another reboot) are showing players how terrifying it can be to face down prehistoric threats, even when well armed. An elevation of Dino Crisis ‘ unique brand of horror is more than enough reason to change its genre this way. The relationship with Resident Evil expands when you think of all that series’ remakes bringing in a new audience.

Ever since Resident Evil 2 Remake , the change to an over-the-shoulder camera similar to RE4 has helped the series thrive, even more than the successful FPS approach in some titles. Should Dino Crisis ever return , it needs to adopt the same plan as Resident Evil , not only to improve its survival horror, but also to streamline mechanics through an inventive genre change.

26edea8a-6789-4e0d-9d5c-9f179ec2c226.title: 2005's Need for Speed ​​Most Wanted gets a cinematic look with DLSS 5 in 4K
26edea8a-6789-4e0d-9d5c-9f179ec2c226.incipit: The iconic racing simulator Need for Speed: Most Wanted has launched in 4K with high-definition textures and the DLSS 5 mod, which eliminates pixel noise on the road and vegetation.
26edea8a-6789-4e0d-9d5c-9f179ec2c226.body:
A detailed gameplay demo of the iconic 2005 arcade racing simulator Need for Speed: Most Wanted, featuring a major visual overhaul, has been released online. The project was launched in native 4K resolution with ultra graphics settings, a reworked high-definition texture pack, and the experimental NVIDIA DLSS 5 neural network rendering technology. In native mode, without modifications, the classic racing game suffers from low-resolution textures, flickering pixel edges on the road, and blurring of distant objects.

The implementation of modern machine learning algorithms has allowed for a complete overhaul of the visuals of this twenty-year-old game, bringing it closer to the standards of modern racing releases. A direct frame-by-frame comparison revealed significant differences in the rendering of the road surface, the surrounding environment, and the sports car. With DLSS 5 disabled, the asphalt appears flat and grainy, cracks in the road surface are lost in pixel noise, and yellow road markings appear double due to insufficient filtering. Enabling neural rendering completely eliminates jaggies: cracks in the asphalt gain volumetric depth and sharp edges, medians become monolithic, and the needles of roadside pines and tree branches are free of subpixel rattle.

On the sports car's body, the glossy paintwork, highlights of the rear lights, and subtle panel gaps are clearly visible without blurring. Activating DLSS 5 also adjusted lighting and atmospheric haze, giving the Rockport suburban highway benchmarks cinematic contrast without distorting the original color gamut. The neural network model reliably reconstructs the fine geometry of bridge guardrails and reinforced concrete tunnel walls at high speeds, preventing the appearance of trails behind the car during maneuvers and skids.

This modification confirmed that the use of generative deep learning algorithms in combination with 4K textures can completely transform the geometry and materials of classic DirectX 9-era games while preserving the original physics model and the dynamics of police chases. b9f36ccb-7a6a-47ae-aea6-20be3b9744f3.title: Star Fox split-screen battle mode update now available
b9f36ccb-7a6a-47ae-aea6-20be3b9744f3.incipit: The big multiplayer update for Star Fox has arrived as promised in the last Nintendo Direct. It adds support for four players locally to play Battle Mode, but those four players can also head online and play...
b9f36ccb-7a6a-47ae-aea6-20be3b9744f3.body:
The big multiplayer update for Star Fox has arrived as promised in the last Nintendo Direct. It adds support for four players locally to play Battle Mode, but those four players can also head online and play against others. There are also three new stages, Katina, Sector X and Venom, added to the game, as well as new items.

But in addition to this new content, there have been a few tweaks to the main game as well, including making it easier to know when you’re damaging certain bosses. The weak point of the Bolse Core boss has also been made more obvious. It’s something we pointed out in our Star Fox review , and we’re glad to see it changed. Aside from that, there are just some other small fixes, which you can find in the full patch notes below.

The Star Fox 1.2.0 update is out now and is, of course, free. In addition to the game’s update, 62 music tracks from the game have also been added to Nintendo Music. Latest update: Ver. 1.2.0 (Released September 29, 2026) Added Elements Battle Mode Added 3 new stages: Katina, Sector X and Venom.

Added new items that appear during battles. The split-screen feature now allows up to four players to play together on a single Nintendo Switch 2 console. A controller is required for each player. When playing split-screen, Joy-Con 2 and Joy-Con controllers can also be used in solo horizontal grip. Added a feature that allows participation in random matches as a team by using the split-screen function.

Changes and Adjustments Campaign Mode / Challenge Mode When you select “ABANDON CAMPAIGN” after getting a game over in Campaign Mode, confirmation dialog will now appear. The visuals have been adjusted to make it easier to see when you are damaging certain bosses. The “Find the hidden power-up in the secret corridor” challenge of “Sector X” has been modified so that it can be completed even if the wing-repair item is obtained. The color of the weak point of the “Bolse Core” boss in “Bolse” has been adjusted.

Battle Mode In Online Battle, the online lobby will not disband after the host leaves. When playing in full screen mode while using a camera in GameChat, the camera feed will now appear on the game screen during matches when you shoot down an enemy aircraft and other instances. A separately sold USB camera is required.

The camera feed and microphone audio are transmitted only to the GameChat members. You can also use character avatars and AR accessories. Training The positions of the goalposts on the left and right sides in the “Use tilt to fly through the goalposts” challenge has been adjusted to make it easier to pass through. Bug fixes Campaign Mode / Challenge Mode Fixed a bug where the game would occasionally crash if the player repeatedly selected RESTART while playing Corneria.

Fixed a bug where, if the player’s ship was shot down at the same time as defeating the boss Bacoon in Aquas, the game would freeze if Bacoon was defeated again after restarting. Fixed a bug where, if the player’s ship was shot down at the same time as defeating the boss Gorgon in Area 6, the game would freeze if Gorgan was defeated again after restarting. Fixed a bug where, in rare cases, the main body of the boss Goras in Titania would not reappear after its arm submerged in the ground, causing the game to freeze.

Fixed a bug where, after playing Venom in Challenge Mode, the game would freeze if the player resumed Campaign Mode from where they left off and cleared Venom. Fixed a bug where, in rare cases, a sound would not play or would play twice after selecting RESTART during gameplay. Fixed a bug in the Zoness challenge “Destroy every Radar Buoy without being spotted” where destroying a Radar Buoy by colliding with it while piloting the Arwing did not result in a failure. Battle Mode Fixed a bug that would occasionally cause the game to crash when starting an Online Battle match. Fixed a bug in Online Battle that would occasionally cause the game to stop progressing normally for the host and remaining participants if the host’s connection was lost.

Fixed a bug where, during a match, when a player’s score exceeded approximately 1200, approximately 1000 points of the score were not correctly calculated. Fixed a bug where the durability of the Arwing’s wings would decrease after playing Challenge Mode on expert difficulty and then playing Battle Mode. Fixed a bug where, after interrupting a play session of Venom 2 and then playing Battle Mode, it sometimes became impossible to perform somersaults or U-turns. Other Changes We have addressed the issue of third-party USB cameras not functioning correctly within the Star Fox game despite working properly on the Nintendo Switch 2 console.

Not all USB cameras are guaranteed to work. If a third-party USB cameras do not work, please use the Nintendo Switch 2 Camera. Fixed several issues to improve the gameplay experience.

0ff1cf8c-b39e-427b-96eb-20d0a840e41e.title: In ICONOLOGY, Painted Thoughts May Crack a Decade-Old Murder
0ff1cf8c-b39e-427b-96eb-20d0a840e41e.incipit: News ICONOLOGY is a crime-suspense adventure for Switch and PC, where an art student uses painted thoughts to investigate her parents’ unsolved murder. GR Staff Editorial...
0ff1cf8c-b39e-427b-96eb-20d0a840e41e.body:
News ICONOLOGY is a crime-suspense adventure for Switch and PC, where an art student uses painted thoughts to investigate her parents’ unsolved murder. GR Staff Editorial Team 30 September 2026 Idea Factory has announced IFChronicle, a new visual-novel brand, and revealed its first game, ICONOLOGY, a crime-suspense adventure planned for Nintendo Switch and PC via Steam. The company has not announced a release date.

Gematsu reported the announcement on September 30. ICONOLOGY follows Haruho Tsubakiya, an art-school student whose parents were murdered in an unsolved crime ten years earlier. Recruited as a Special Investigator for her ability to decipher cognitive paintings, she uses the White Cube, a device that renders suspects’ thoughts as images, to investigate their motives and trauma. Choices, relationships with fellow investigators and interpretations of the paintings can shape the story’s multiple endings.

Scenario writer Makoto Fukami, whose credits include the PSYCHO-PASS anime series and the films Resident Evil: Vendetta and Resident Evil: Death Island, is working on the game. Character designs come from Teita, whose credits include Fate/Grand Order and CharadeManiacs. The listed language options are English, Japanese, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese.

The premise puts psychological clues at the centre of its investigation. IFChronicle’s first reveal establishes the brand’s focus on narrative adventures, with international language support confirmed for its debut title. a3a8264a-4979-482f-8aed-86aba123b909.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Returns to the Series' Best-Ever Era
a3a8264a-4979-482f-8aed-86aba123b909.incipit: Intelligent Systems figured out how to modernize its decades-old formula at last Image: Intelligent Systems/Nintendo via Polygon Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave might have all the trappings of a modern Fire Emblem, with its Engage -like personal skills an
a3a8264a-4979-482f-8aed-86aba123b909.body:
Intelligent Systems figured out how to modernize its decades-old formula at last Image: Intelligent Systems/Nintendo via Polygon Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave might have all the trappings of a modern Fire Emblem, with its Engage -like personal skills and the social elements of Three Houses . But behind those Kurahana-illustrated eyes is the soul of a classic Fire Emblem game. The latest installment of the series shows Intelligent Systems at its most confident, having finally found a way to harmonize its classic systems with modern expectations.

You could've told me Fortune's Weave was Intelligent Systems' Fire Emblem anniversary project, and I'd believe it. It's crammed with little homages pulled from throughout the series, but tweaked to function more like an evolution, proof of how far the series has come in 30 years. The biggest one is how characters relate to each other. Gone are the days where every character has to have a dozen support conversation partners and romance interests.

Not that it was always bad. Fates and Three Houses had quite a few excellent pairings. A lot of them felt forced, though, like Intelligent Systems was overcompensating for how dull and limited Radiant Dawn 's supports were back in 2006.

Fortune's Weave calls to mind the Game Boy Advance era of Fire Emblem. Every character has a handful of support conversations with people who truly matter to them — colleagues, family members, rivals, occasionally a random clash of two big personalities. Romance is a thing, but it, and the making of time-traveling baby warriors, aren't the only thing. It even does my favorite thing from that early ‘00s period of Fire Emblem, where a handful of random, mysterious outlier characters sport excellent stats and great designs that make you want to know more about them (like Legault or Farina), but have maybe five conversation partners if you're lucky. Relationships feel more intimate and meaningful this way, not like lore dumps.

You don't have to tell me everything about every character's life! Just the bits that mean something to their story, please. And the payoff is worth it. Even Nuzzuo, who has one support chat with one person, benefits from the depth it brings to him, which you wouldn't otherwise get from the brief moment he appears in Cai's path.

The underworld plot deserves a special shout-out, too. Undead monsters and evil underworld lords are hardly new to Fire Emblem, but I was always disappointed how impersonal they often felt. 2004's Sacred Stones was the only game that wove personality in with the netherworld stuff. Fortune's Weave does it too, turning it into a twisted family drama that traces itself all the way back to Sothis' arrival centuries before.

It elevates the plot so much more. And giving undead enemies special powers adds a sense of challenge you were supposed to feel going up against skeleton armies in Sacred Stones , but only really got when the giant zombie dragons showed up. Image: Intelligent Systems/Nintendo Then there's fog of war (limited vision). Three Houses and Engage had it, to an extent, but the maps that featured it were a far cry from the memorable likes of Blazing Blade 's "Battle before Dawn" or some of Radiant Dawn 's more challenging maps.

The tension just wasn't there. The fog maps in Fortune's Weave carry a sense of danger, even the smaller skirmish-type maps. Enemies behave in such a brutal fashion, seeking out targets they're effective against and surrounding them, that not knowing where they are or what they're packing feels like a serious threat.

There's a blessing to mitigate restricted vision, if you’re finding it makes things too hard, but more importantly, there's a small network of other interactions that makes these low-vis maps even more interesting than the earlier ones that inspired them. Discovering an enemy makes them confused for a turn, which means they can't counterattack. There's also a set of accessories that grants you extra buffs when you attack confused enemies, so you can invoke the blessing, expand your vision, confuse a whole mob of enemies, then sweep in and demolish them. In the same vein, doing away with the weapon triangle and durability issues may look like concessions to modernity, but I see it more as a long-overdue improvement. Building functions into weapons instead of classes — like axes always hitting hard at the cost of accuracy or swords being stronger with follow-ups — leaves more room for strategic flexibility.

The result is the same, essentially. You're thinking about which character's skills work best with your chosen weapons and who needs to be there to support them. But you have so many more options for what that looks like instead of using the same swordmasters, knights, and paladins the same way every time.

After years of experiments like weapon wear and adding debuffs to strong weapons in Fates , it plays like Intelligent Systems finally figured out how to make its classic systems work in a modern setting.

4a9917fd-4b2a-4106-a57e-ffadbd886ed2.title: Evidence of canceled Grand Theft Auto 5 Liberty City and 'Agent Trevor' DLC, plus early version of GTA6's map surface online
4a9917fd-4b2a-4106-a57e-ffadbd886ed2.incipit: When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.Credit: RockstarAs reported by IGN, a trove of data from Rockstar has made its way online, with the big...
4a9917fd-4b2a-4106-a57e-ffadbd886ed2.body:
When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission. Credit: Rockstar As reported by IGN , a trove of data from Rockstar has made its way online, with the big ticket items being Grand Theft Auto 5's source code, remnants of canceled GTA5 singleplayer DLC, as well as an early version of GTA6's map that can be loaded into the prior game. It's unclear how or why the data is making the rounds now, but the consensus appears to be that it was first extracted from Rockstar in the infamous 2022 Lapsus hack that revealed GTA6 to the world.

GTA YouTuber TJGM has a video and a number of posts on X covering the long-rumored Liberty City project . The gameplay in the video comes from a canceled mod, and not the leaked material. The most notable thing TJGM showed off is a map of audio loading zones contained in the leak: The demarcation for coastal ambient audio could be turned into an effective map of the multi-island city. This iteration of Liberty City would have been larger, and possessed a different layout from its most recent predecessor in GTA4.

User affmal on Twitter has been sharing screenshots and findings mostly focused on the Agent Trevor files, which appear to be more intact and substantial than the Liberty City stuff. Affmal has shared a full mission list , and has been loading map and model data into GTA5 to explore. The coolest thing affmal has shown off, for my money, is an underwater base map like something out of Deus Ex.

TJGM has a few posts showing screenshots of an early version of GTA6's map loaded into GTA5, with markers (unclear if from Rockstar for dev purposes or placed by the user) denoting areas like "Alligator Farm," "Coast Guard," and "Disused Theme Park." The map is "very unfinished" according to TJGM, and reportedly dates to 2015. He has three posts showing corresponding locations from this unfinished map and GTA6's trailers side-by-side for comparison. This is only the latest development in a GTA6 build-up that has been defined by major leaks, and it's possible there is still more to be uncovered in this tranche. GTA6 itself will finally release on November 19, but not on PC. While Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick acknowledged that " the PC platform is becoming more and more important " in a recent meeting, there's still no word on when we can expect the hotly anticipated crime sim on our system of choice.

03d3a74d-3629-4cc4-8890-1952660aa355.title: Diablo IV and PoE 2 competitor to get fifth season - Last Epoch new content trailer
03d3a74d-3629-4cc4-8890-1952660aa355.incipit: Diablo IV and PoE 2 competitor to get fifth season - The ARPG developers are preparing new content and...
03d3a74d-3629-4cc4-8890-1952660aa355.body:
Diablo IV and PoE 2 competitor to get fifth season - The ARPG developers are preparing new content and mechanics. Recently, Eleventh Hour Games studio reminded about itself again. Now the developers of Last Epoch are preparing to launch the fifth season and they have published a trailer dedicated to the upcoming innovations.

Last Epoch will feature the boss Morditas, God of Bloodshed; a new seasonal mechanic "Rage of Morditas" and several additional skills will be added; various QoL improvements will be introduced, such as a new interface for "activities", as well as new item sets. The release of Last Epoch's fifth season "Rage of the Frostborn" is scheduled for October 1, 2026. The developers have not yet published a detailed description of the innovations: they are going to start sharing additional details from September 21. Источник изображения: Eleventh Hour Games, KRAFTON, Inc Since the release of the full version of Last Epoch, the project's audience has significantly decreased. At the time of the 1.0 release, the ARPG's online presence on Steam exceeded 264 thousand players, while recently the peak online has been at the level of 1 – 1.5 thousand users.

Overall, Last Epoch has "mostly positive" reviews, with a rating of 76% after more than 118 thousand user reviews.

d5c565ef-2734-4675-880d-8a89b23a8dfb.title: Montgomery Parks and Rec. to host community gaming tournament
d5c565ef-2734-4675-880d-8a89b23a8dfb.incipit: Young gamers will have a chance to put their skills to the test for a shot at cash prizes.The Montgomery Parks and Recreation Department will host a gaming tournament on Friday,...
d5c565ef-2734-4675-880d-8a89b23a8dfb.body:
MONTGOMERY, Ala. ( WSFA ) - Young gamers will have a chance to put their skills to the test for a shot at cash prizes. The Montgomery Parks and Recreation Department will host a gaming tournament on Friday, Sept. 25, from 5:30 p.m. to 8 p.m. at the Chisholm Community Center, 545 East Vandiver Boulevard. It is open to players 13 and older of all skill levels.

The competition features two gaming brackets: Fortnite and Super Smash Bros. The Fortnite winner will receive a $100 GameStop gift card, and the Super Smash Bros. champion will receive a $50 GameStop gift card. The entry fee is $10 per player. Participants may scan the QR code on the event flyer or register through the city’s website .

Registration closes Sept. 24 at 5 p.m. Young gamers will have a chance to put their skills to the test for a shot at cash prizes. (Source: Montgomery Parks and Recreation Department) Department officials emphasize their expectations for all players to display good sportsmanship to ensure a positive atmosphere. For more details, call the Parks and Recreation Department at 344-659-7681.

d65b0f78-f575-4376-93db-1b8353cfb34a.title: Typhoon Dujuan Forces Tokyo Game Show 2026 To Shut Down A Day Early
d65b0f78-f575-4376-93db-1b8353cfb34a.incipit: Tokyo Game Show 2026 was supposed to be the first time in the gaming expo’s history that it would run for five days. Unfortunately, the festivities are being cut a day short as Japan braces for Typhoon...
d65b0f78-f575-4376-93db-1b8353cfb34a.body:
Tokyo Game Show 2026 was supposed to be the first time in the gaming expo’s history that it would run for five days. Unfortunately, the festivities are being cut a day short as Japan braces for Typhoon Dujuan. “Due to the approach of Typhoon No. 25, strong winds and rain are expected to intensify in the afternoon and beyond, and disruptions to transportation are also a concern,” the event organizers announced on X on September 19.

“Therefore, prioritizing the safety of all attendees, exhibitors, and related parties, as well as ensuring safe return home, we have decided to cancel the event for the entire day. We sincerely apologize to everyone who was looking forward to attending for this unfortunate news.” TGS、5時から入場待ち可能なはずなのに5時丁度に着いてこれ。 時間守れないオタクがたーくさん! この感じだと4時とか徹夜で並んでる人もいるんじゃないー? 守ってるのバカらしいから徹夜しようかしら〜?? #TGS2026 pic.twitter.com/qDDU60NpmA — Aran🪽💧🌙🏫🥀🦋🫘💊 (@Arangeme1999412) September 18, 2026 While the event will continue as scheduled on September 20 amid the storm’s approach, all attendees will be refunded for September 21. It’s unclear how that might work for all of the game developers who purchased booth space for the full five days. Tokyo Game Show 2026 marks the event’s 30th anniversary, and with a holiday falling on September 21 in Japan this year, the decision was made to expand the gaming convention to a fifth day.

While the show has been light on big new announcements and game reveals, the show floor has been packed with several publishers putting up elaborate booths. タコで すみません。 pic.twitter.com/qJWB2r87zn — 社畜さん (@cquall_cos) September 19, 2026 The Square Enix section included a brand-new hands-on demo for Final Fantasy VII Revelation with a giant statue of Sephiroth holding out his sword Masamune preparing to stab the ground hanging overtop. PlayStation, meanwhile, was hosting large screenings of the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look trailer complete with IRL special effects to enhance the presentation. “As a result [of Typhoon No. 25], the hands-on demos and streaming events scheduled for September 21 (Monday, holiday) at the PlayStation booth will also be canceled,” Sony announced on X today.

“We regret to inform everyone who was looking forward to it, but we kindly ask for your understanding.” Typhoon Dujuan is expected to approach Japan’s Kanto region, including Tokyo, around Monday night, local time. The Japan Meteorological Agency is forecasting wind speeds that could reach up to 78 miles per hour.
